categories.title: Crypto Market Conditions: Bear vs Bull Debate and Alt Season Discussion

content.text: On July 23, 2026, users in the discussion channel debated whether the crypto market is currently in a bear or bull market. One user argued it remains a bear market until the top 100 coins by market cap each reach at least 1 billion dollars in market capitalization, referencing conditions seen in late 2020 and mid 2025 as benchmarks for a true bull market. Another user countered that major cap coins like Ethereum are in a bear market and that everything else is just noise. A third user pushed back on both, stating that crypto is no longer a small market where everything moves together, and that it now moves in sectors. This user pointed to onchain markets, specifically the Robinhood chain, as currently experiencing a bull market, while majors lag behind. The conversation also touched on Ethereum not having had a meaningful bull run in over five years, only recently breaking above its 2021 high in August 2025. Users attributed this partly to a poor macro environment and tightening monetary policy over the past five years. The discussion also noted that past narratives such as AI coins, meme coins following the 2024 presidential election, RWA, and the Robinhood chain have each drawn attention in cycles, similar to how attention drove the semiconductor stock market. One user expressed doubt that a broad alt season like 2021 would return, while another insisted alt season is already happening in specific sectors and that participants are missing the point by focusing only on majors. The conversation briefly extended to rising memory and smartphone prices as a reflection of broader macro pressures, with one user humorously suggesting that cheap memory prices might signal the return of a broad alt season.

In the general discussion channel, several topics came up throughout the day. Sam announced that a Zeroclaw community call was live, inviting members interested in how the project supports the broader crypto ecosystem. A user named Faouzi122 raised a technical question directed at developers building AI agents that allocate capital into liquidity pool positions, asking how they handle impermanent loss calculations and breakeven points before committing funds to a pool, specifically whether they hardcode formulas, use an SDK, or skip the check entirely. The question was framed as an attempt to determine if this is a genuine ongoing pain point in the space. A user named Angelina directed criticism at project leadership, tagging moderators Shaw and Kenk, claiming the project's decline began before the bear market due to immature leadership. Shagun asked who to contact regarding listing proposals, receiving a dismissive reaction from other members. Troseddol and Mint from Action Model both reached out seeking partnership contacts, with Mint specifically identifying themselves as representing Action Model and asking how to pursue partnership discussions.

A solo builder operating under the handle agentshare.dev announced they are developing an API-first data platform focused on real-time Solana DeFi intelligence. The platform provides Meteora DLMM pool briefs, bin depth data, and DEX scouting capabilities. The project is described as fully x402-ready, meaning it is designed to support autonomous agents and micro-billing use cases.

A user named NativeSatoshi announced the launch of Coopa v4.0, a data sovereignty platform built on top of Irys for permanent and immutable data storage. The platform is described as a zero-trust Digital Sanctuary aimed at professional users, offering wallet-based identity, closed-source cryptographic protection, and a feature called Eternal Whispers for sovereign data interaction and messaging. Coopa is normally invite-only but was temporarily opened to the Irys community for stress-testing. Feedback was requested specifically on Irys upload speeds, wallet integration UI, and the overall platform experience. The platform is accessible at coopaassistant.com.

In the general discussion channel, community members touched on several topics on July 27, 2026. A notable mention was made that Storj has filed for bankruptcy, while Eliza continues its development work. A new member named deedee joined the server and expressed that token values have dropped significantly, making selling tokens less worthwhile. A user named Ginga posted asking if anyone is looking to hire a developer, and separately, another user named so posted a request specifically seeking a U.S.-based software developer with at least five years of experience, asking interested parties to send a direct message. General greetings were exchanged among members in the evening hours. The coders channel had no activity recorded for the same date.

categories.title: ElizaOS Token Community Sentiment and Project Activity Discussion

content.text: On July 28, 2026, community members in the ElizaOS Discord discussion channel expressed significant concern and frustration over the dramatic decline of the Eliza token, which had fallen from a peak market cap of approximately 2.4 billion dollars down to around 4 million dollars. Several users described the token as effectively dead with no clear path to recovery. One user noted that the only visible signs of ongoing development were GitHub commits, with lead developer Shaw reportedly active only on GitHub and not posting content directly related to ElizaOS on other platforms. Despite the bearish sentiment, at least one user disclosed they made a speculative purchase at the low price point, while another mentioned having inherited the token from the earlier ai16z era and having profited from a short trade. Questions were raised about whether the token is listed on any major exchanges beyond Kraken, and whether there were any meaningful announcements or signs of life from the team. One community member noted that an app appeared to be ready but questioned why there was no promotion of it on the main social media presence. The overall tone of the conversation reflected deep skepticism about the token's future value, with participants largely agreeing that only GitHub activity remained as evidence of any ongoing work.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion: Project Communication Concerns, Lawsuit Update, and Developer Announcements

content.text: In the general discussion channel, community members expressed significant frustration over the lack of public communication from the ElizaOS team. User paolin raised concerns that while development activity is visible on GitHub and Shaw has posted occasionally on X about the Eliza app, all other official channels including Discord, X, and Farcaster have been largely inactive since late May. Paolin argued that the absence of regular updates is causing outsiders to assume the project is dead, and that this silence is damaging to community trust and potential investor interest. Paolin also noted that Shaw had previously pinned messages stating both Milady and Eliza v3 were nearing completion, but those milestones have not been publicly delivered, with no release date announced for the Eliza app. Paolin also suggested a token utility model where users would need to purchase and lock up ElizaOS tokens to access plugins and services, as a potential funding mechanism. User J_CHOY pushed back, arguing the team is actively building and shipping, pointing to GitHub activity and Shaw's posts on X as evidence. The exchange became heated, with both parties trading insults before other members called for more respectful dialogue. Separately, paolin shared a court document indicating that the lawsuit involving plaintiff Gorka Pikabea and the appearing defendants was dismissed with prejudice following a settlement, with the court retaining jurisdiction for 30 days to enforce the agreement, signed by Judge Jed S. Rakoff on July 8, 2026. User Omid Sa clarified that Eliza V3 was released some time ago and has been receiving updates, and can be accessed by cloning the main repository. Omid Sa also publicly requested that Shaw consider reinstating community member odlitime to the Discord. User Bek posted asking if anyone was looking for a developer.

In the coders channel, two external project announcements were made. User Kenhinde announced the launch of Coopa v4.0, described as a zero-trust digital data sovereignty platform built on top of Irys for permanent and immutable data storage. The platform uses wallet-based identity, requires no traditional cloud storage, and features a proprietary cryptographic layer. It is normally invite-only but was temporarily opened to the Irys community for stress testing, with feedback requested on upload speeds, wallet integration, and overall user experience. The platform is accessible at coopaassistant.com. Additionally, user x402 Data Hub announced the launch of x402 Data Hub, a real-time data API designed for autonomous AI agents. It provides access to LLM latency data, AI API pricing, cloud GPU rental indexes, and gas rates via HTTP 402 micro-payments at 0.01 USDC on Base and Arbitrum networks, with no API keys or signups required. Fifty free daily requests per dataset are available for developer testing.
